subject: Archer onboarding: evidence snapshot & S3 presign artifacts
messages:
From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@brightleaf.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Archer intake — initial evidence snapshot & presign question

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier this week. Brightleaf is starting the Archer onboarding and our security team is working through the evidence items. Two quick asks to unblock our intake: 

1) Can you send a small evidence snapshot (SOC 2 high-level summary + one sample policy) we can attach to the Archer profile so reviewers have immediate context?

2) We saw references to Redwood using S3 presigned uploads for large artifacts in other customers' Archer submissions. Can you confirm what audit/log artifacts you can provide to demonstrate possession of uploaded files (e.g., presign request logs, upload completion receipts, signed etags)? Our GCP/S3 onboarding checklist requires those for ingestion.

If helpful, we can open an Archer ticket and grant you upload access; otherwise we can accept a sample ZIP via secure transfer for intake.

I can be reached on +1-415-555-0198 if a quick call is easier.

Thanks,
Lydia Park
Security Program Manager
Brightleaf Health
[Attachment: Brightleaf-scope.pdf (PDF, 48KB)]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@brightleaf.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Archer intake — initial evidence snapshot & presign question

Hi Lydia — appreciate the detail. Short answers up front and a proposal for the handoff: 

- Evidence snapshot: attaching a 1-page SOC 2 summary and a sample Access Control policy that reviewers can consume immediately.
- S3 presign artifacts: we can provide a presign request log (timestamp, requestor id, object key template), the presign response metadata, and an upload completion log that includes the object ETag and checksum. For Archer ingestion we usually include an "upload manifest" (CSV) that maps each evidence filename to a presign id and upload receipt.

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan):
1) I will upload a minimal evidence bundle directly into the Archer ticket you open (or we can use the secure transfer link you prefer).
2) David will perform a quick scrub to remove any PII from the sample artifacts before we hand them off.
3) Ben will follow up on retention TTL expectations and confirm retention metadata we should include with each artifact.

Attached: redwood_s3_presign_guidance.pdf (short doc), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf.

If Archer access is already open, please add support@redwood.com as an uploader role in AR-4723 (I believe that's the ticket number you mentioned on the call). Otherwise, send a secure transfer link and we'll push the bundle there.

Best,

Tessa Morgan
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_s3_presign_guidance.pdf (PDF, 220KB)]
[Attachment: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (PDF, 96KB)]

From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@brightleaf.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 13:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Archer intake — initial evidence snapshot & presign question

Thanks Tessa — that plan works. A couple of clarifications: 

- Retention TTL: our reviewers want to see a retention field on each artifact (e.g., 1 year / 3 years / indefinite). Would Redwood include retention metadata in the upload manifest?

- Evidence redaction: when you say "scrub to remove PII," can you confirm whether the scrub is automated or manual and whether you can supply a short note describing the redaction process for the record? We occasionally receive evidence with residual account ids and need to be explicit in the profile about redaction steps.

- DocuSign: we prefer a signed attestation PDF from your security lead for profile finalization. If you can route a DocuSign request to security@brightleaf.com, we can complete the signature step.

Also forwarded the Archer ticket link to your team.

Date: Sat, 02 Jun 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Archer intake — evidence bundle uploaded to AR-4723

Hi Lydia — quick update: we pushed a minimal evidence bundle into AR-4723 this morning and attached the upload manifest and scrub note. Items uploaded:

- redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (summary page)
- sample_access_control_policy.pdf (redacted)
- upload_manifest.csv (maps filenames to presign ids and upload receipts)
- presign_request_log.csv (timestamps + requestor ids)
- archer-upload-log.txt (upload receipts + ETags)
- redaction_note.txt (manual review checklist and tools used)

For traceability we included retention metadata in upload_manifest.csv — default TTL set to "3 years" for this bundle, with an explicit retention column you can edit per artifact.

I've requested DocuSign for the attestation from our Head of Security; you'll receive an envelope from dseals@redwood.com shortly. David will join a short handoff call if you want to walk through the manifest and evidentiary fields (I'm proposing 30 minutes next Tue at 10:00 PT).

Related links: AR ticket https://archer.example.com/ticket/AR-4723 ; HubSpot deal https://app.hubspot.com/deal/HS-9182 (internal tracking).

If you need the bundle sent to a secure transfer location instead of attaching to Archer, let us know and we'll push the ZIP.

Cheers,

Tessa Morgan
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
